## Your landings data

This lesson runs against **your country's landing records** — the same data, with the
same access permissions, as the Data Download tab. It is loaded into the R environment
below as a data frame called `landings`.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Fetch the signed-in user's capped, permission-filtered landings as JSON, reusing the
// exact API base URL the React app computed (apiConfig.getApiBaseUrl), which it publishes
// to localStorage on load. This makes the lesson behave like the Data Download tab in
// both dev (-> http://localhost:3001/api) and prod (-> same-origin /api). The lesson
// shares the app's origin, so the JWT in localStorage is available here too.
landings_data = {
  const token = localStorage.getItem("authToken");
  if (!token) return [];
  const apiBase = localStorage.getItem("apiBaseUrl") || "/api";
  const res = await fetch(`${apiBase}/data-download/explorer-data`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, Accept: "application/json" }
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    console.warn(`explorer-data fetch failed: ${res.status}`);
    return [];
  }
  return await res.json();
}
```

```{webr}
#| autorun: true
#| input:
#|   - landings_data
# quarto-live converts the JS array of row objects (landings_data) into an R
# data.frame automatically; guard the empty / not-signed-in case.
landings <- tryCatch(as.data.frame(landings_data), error = function(e) data.frame())

cat("Rows loaded:", nrow(landings), "  Columns:", ncol(landings), "\n")
head(landings)
```

## Try it yourself

`landings` is available in every cell on this page. Run or edit the cell below:

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
str(landings)
```
